How to move through the menu

With no screen reader, drag your finger over the screen: each choice takes a band and is said as you pass it. Lift your finger to choose the one you hear. If you keep your finger still, you hear its explanation. With the volume keys: volume down goes to the next choice, volume up to the previous one, and holding a key chooses. The last choice of each page is Back; on the main page, Leave the rescue.
How to come back to the rescue

Hold both volume keys for a few seconds, if you assigned the shortcut to Accessible Rescue. With the guardian on, or outside the menu during a rescue, press volume up three times quickly. You can also open the Accessible Rescue app or the Rescue tile in quick settings.

It starts with three quick presses of volume up. With the advanced permission it turns every screen reader off and the menu speaks with its own voice. If you leave without turning one on, or a few seconds pass without touching anything, your screen reader turns back on. Without the permission, it starts echo mode.

When TalkBack or another screen reader is on but silent, for example because the system voice broke, the rescue reads with its own voice whatever that screen reader focuses. You keep using your usual gestures.

Touch or drag to hear what is there. Double tap activates. Swipe right, next item; left, previous. Swipe down or up to scroll the list. Down then left, back. Up then left, home. Right then down, notifications. Up then down, read the whole screen. Two fingers to scroll.

Android only lets an app turn screen readers on or off and change the speech engine with a permission granted once, with a computer, with the phone\'s own wireless debugging, or with root. With it, the rescue does it at once. Without it, the rescue guides you through Settings.
